summary:
ASTROQUEST is an interactive educational web application designed for children aged 8–12. It introduces young learners to astronaut life and space exploration through an engaging lunar and Mars mission simulation.

Players take on the role of mission controllers and make decisions about essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, power and radiation protection. Their decisions influence the mission's progress and success.

The project aims to make space science more accessible and enjoyable through interactive learning and decision-making.
details:
About the Project

ASTROQUEST – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational web application designed to introduce children and young learners to the challenges of astronaut life and space exploration.

How Does It Work?

The application allows users to begin a simulated space mission by selecting a destination, such as the Moon or Mars. During the mission, players take responsibility for managing essential resources, including oxygen, water, food, power and radiation protection.

Users encounter different mission situations and make decisions to maintain crew safety and complete their objectives. Their decisions influence resource availability and the overall mission outcome. At the end, users receive a mission score based on their performance.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Makes space science and astronaut activities more engaging and accessible.
  • Encourages critical thinking and decision-making.
  • Introduces resource management and problem-solving concepts.
  • Helps young learners understand the importance of safety and teamwork during space missions.
  • Promotes curiosity about space exploration.

Technologies Used

The application was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. HTML structures the application, CSS provides the visual design and styling, and JavaScript handles the interactive mission logic, resource management and decision-making system.

Creativity and Innovation

ASTROQUEST transforms space exploration concepts into an interactive learning experience. Instead of only reading about astronaut activities, users actively participate in a simulated mission where their decisions influence the outcome.

The project combines educational content, space exploration and game-based learning in a beginner-friendly environment.
